title: Targeted cancer drugs: antibodies and checkpoint blockers
ariaLabel: Schematic of four cancer targets: growth factor receptors such as HER2 drive tumour cell division, VEGF drives new blood vessels, CD20 marks B cells for destruction, and PD-1 lets tumours switch off T cells. Trastuzumab blocks HER2, bevacizumab blocks VEGF, rituximab targets CD20 cells, and pembrolizumab frees T cells by blocking PD-1.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Tumour cell division
nodes.info: Cell division driven by the HER2 signal.

nodes.label: VEGF signal
nodes.info: Vascular endothelial growth factor made by tumours to grow new vessels.

nodes.label: CD20 B cells
nodes.info: B cells that carry the CD20 marker.

nodes.label: PD-1 brake
nodes.info: PD-1 is a brake on T cells that tumours use by showing PD-L1.

nodes.label: T cell brake
nodes.info: The PD-1 brake that switches T cells off.

nodes.label: Tumour activity
nodes.info: A teaching score for tumour growth and escape from immune attack.

edges.label: HER2 receptor
edges.info: Trastuzumab binds HER2, blocks its signalling and marks the cell for immune attack.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: VEGF
edges.info: Bevacizumab binds VEGF so the tumour gets less new blood supply.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: CD20 target
edges.info: Rituximab binds CD20 and these cells are destroyed by antibody-dependent and complement-dependent killing.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: PD-1 pathway
edges.info: Pembrolizumab and nivolumab block PD-1, so T cells are released from the brake and can attack the tumour. Blocking the brake raises immune-related adverse effects.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Trastuzumab blocks HER2, bevacizumab blocks VEGF, rituximab targets CD20 cells, and pembrolizumab blocks PD-1. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib, EGFR and ALK drugs, CAR-T cells, biomarkers and who is eligible, combination regimens, immune-related adverse effects, cardiotoxicity of trastuzumab, infusion reactions and cost are left out. Tumour activity is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
